## Findings
- claim-1: RWY Theorem 4.8, over \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), gives both the right-adjoined family \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) and lower-adjoined family \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) as generators of \(J_v\), where \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-876]
- claim-2: RWY Conjecture 4.10 says both Theorem 4.8 generating sets are minimal, rather than stating minimality as a theorem. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 938-946]
- claim-3: St. Dizier–Yong Theorem 1.2, for \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), and \(b=\min(i,j)\), proves minimality only of \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) in \(H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
- claim-4: Corollary 4.6 again concludes minimality only for the lower-adjoined family. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 827-831]
- claim-5: Remark 4.7 identifies \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) as the conjugate/right-adjoined family and says one “could straightforwardly” transpose the arguments; it states neither a transposed theorem nor a corollary. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]
- claim-6: For the inspected full-text sources, the requested target is established: no separately stated right-family minimality theorem was found; transposition is proposed in a remark and must be proved if used. This is a bounded negative result, not a claim about all literature.
## Strategy
Compare RWY Theorem 4.8 and Conjecture 4.10 with St. Dizier–Yong Theorem 1.2, Corollary 4.6, and Remark 4.7. RWY proves integral generation of both families, but conjectures minimality [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-876; 938-946]. The 2024 theorem and corollary prove only lower-adjoined-family minimality [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235; 827-831]. Remark 4.7 identifies the right-adjoined family and proposes transposition of the arguments, without stating a theorem [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840].

Thus the requested target is established relative to the inspected sources: no separately stated theorem of **right-family minimality** was found. Any use of transposition for that conclusion requires an internal proof, not attribution to these sources.

## Gaps
This is a bounded negative result for RWY (2011) and St. Dizier–Yong (2024), not a universal claim about all literature. It does not deny the source-backed right-family generation theorem.
